title: Coursive plugin manifest, version 3
description: Accepted shape of a Coursive plugin manifest: the package.json document of a plugin package, whose "coursive" key declares the plugin. This file is the authority for the fields it names; contribution entries keep the group-specific fields that spec 0032 defines, and the plugin's settings form keeps the subset that spec 0004 defines.

name.description: Package name, for display and provenance only.

version.description: Semantic version of the plugin itself.

api.description: Plugin API range the plugin needs: ^x.y.z, >=x.y.z or an exact version. The host rejects a range it does not satisfy.

serviceId.description: Service identity as domain.verb, for example transcript.read.

serviceRange.description: Required service version range: ^1, ^1.2.3, >=1.0.0 or an exact version.

contributionId.description: Identity of one contribution within its group; unique per group and stable across versions.

relativePath.description: Path inside the plugin package: no absolute path, no drive letter, no backslash, no empty, dot or dot-dot segment, no trailing slash. A leading ./ is allowed and normalized away.

entry.description: One package-relative entry path, or one path per platform key (linux-x64, linux-arm64, windows-x64, macos-x64, macos-arm64) for a process runtime.

runtime.description: One runtime component of the plugin. A plugin may declare several, in different engines.

kind.description: pi: the Node assistant host; moejs: the optional Go script executor; process: a supervised native or JSON-RPC program; web-ui: static assets rendered in an isolated WebView; go: a daemon built-in module.

skills.description: Pi runtime only: package-relative SKILL.md directories or files the assistant host offers as a playbook.

optional.description: When true, the plugin keeps its other components if this one cannot run here.

requirement.description: A service the plugin needs before its contributions can activate.

optional.description: When true, a missing provider selects the plugin's documented degraded mode instead of blocking it.

provision.description: A service the plugin provides to other plugins and to the agent.

contribution.description: One entry of a contribution group. Group-specific fields (surface, target, route, renderer, order, scope and so on) belong to spec 0032; this schema fixes the shared identity rule that duplicate detection depends on.

protocol.description: Source-provider protocol version the executable speaks.

executable.description: One program per platform key: linux-x64, linux-arm64, windows-x64, macos-x64 or macos-arm64.

navigation.description: Navigation entries; each names the page it opens.

pages.description: Complete pages with a renderer and a fallback.

slots.description: Entries for a typed UI slot; the target names the slot.

tools.description: Agent tools, each identified by the service it exposes.

views.description: Interactive views the plugin's results and blocks may carry.

actions.description: Actions the app can invoke for this plugin.

settings.description: Sections this plugin adds to the settings surface.

sources.description: Content sources: the sign-in, course and media surface a source-provider executable offers (spec 0024).

id.description: Stable plugin identity, also the install directory name and the tool-name prefix.

icon.description: A Material Symbols name, or a package-relative PNG, WebP or SVG path of at most 256 KiB.

exec.description: Commands the exec permission allows, each an absolute path or a name on PATH.

hosts.description: Host names the network permission allows.

settings.description: The plugin's settings form, in the JSON Schema subset spec 0004 defines.
